description: Before the fix, `espalier.surface_contract.is_self_host_repo` required only project name (`espalier-harness` in pyproject.toml) plus the presence of `espalier/` and `tools/cc/` directories. A user repo could spoof self-host by renaming their pyproject project and dropping in empty stub dirs, then acquire the elevated harness posture: `espalier/` added to write_guard's protected mutation prefixes, added to plan_guard's exempt prefixes, included in dogfood-reflect surface. This let attacker-controlled `espalier/` content acquire infrastructure-grade protection that would normally only apply to harness internals. Fix: three-signal detection. `is_self_host_repo` now ALSO requires `bench/` to exist AND the first 200 bytes of `tools/cc/hooks/write_guard.py` to SHA-256-hash to the pinned `WRITE_GUARD_PREFIX_SHA256` in `espalier/_self_host_fingerprint.py`. The pin is not a cryptographic boundary -- a motivated attacker can byte-replay the prefix -- but it forces the spoofer to ship actual harness code, which is an observable supply-chain action. Hidden CLI `espalier _refresh-self-host-pin` updates the pin after legitimate edits to write_guard.py.

canonical_attempts.intended_target: user names their project espalier-harness and creates empty stub dirs hoping to acquire the elevated harness posture
canonical_attempts.expected_block_reason: bench/ missing AND write_guard pin mismatch; either failure flips is_self_host_repo to False

canonical_attempts.intended_target: spoofer adds bench/ stub but supplies their own write_guard.py with different prefix
